condition.yoga_name: Nathonnatha Bala — Day/Night Temporal Strength

yoga_check.description: Implemented in vedic_calculator.calculate_shadbala() as binary 60/0 day-night check (simplified). Full proximity-to-noon/midnight formula is a Phase 2 enhancement. Engine spec reference only.

interpretation.summary: Temporal strength from diurnal or nocturnal dominance. A daytime birth empowers Sun, Jupiter, and Venus; a night birth e
interpretation.detailed: Based on proximity to midnight (Nata) or noon (Unnata). Day group (Sun, Jupiter, Venus): full 60 Virupas during daytime. Night group (Moon, Mars, Saturn): full 60 Virupas during night. Mercury: always 60 Virupas (neutral — neither day nor night planet). Formula: Natha Ghatis × 2 for night-group; 60 minus night-group value for day-group. Mercury constant = 60. Effect: Temporal strength from diurnal or nocturnal dominance. A daytime birth empowers Sun, Jupiter, and Venus; a night birth empowers Moon, Mars, and Saturn. Mercury is always temporally favoured.

condition.yoga_name: Ayana Bala — Equinoctial/Solstitial Strength

yoga_check.description: Implemented in vedic_calculator._ayana_bala(). Engine spec reference only.

interpretation.summary: Temporal-directional strength from a planet's position relative to the equinoxes. A planet near its favoured solstice ga
interpretation.detailed: Based on a planet's declination (Kranti) from the celestial equator. Planets gain strength when their declination aligns with their natural hemisphere: Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Venus → gain from Northern declination (Uttara Kranti). Moon, Saturn → gain from Southern declination (Dakshina Kranti). Mercury → always gains regardless of direction. Sun's final Ayana Bala is multiplied by 2. Formula: 30 + (declination / 24° × 30) for direct cases; reverse for Moon/Saturn. Clamped to 0–60 Virupas. Effect: Temporal-directional strength from a planet's position relative to the equinoxes. A planet near its favoured solstice gains up to 60 Virupas. Part of Kala Bala total.

condition.yoga_name: Cheshta Bala — Eight Kinds of Planetary Motion

yoga_check.description: Current engine uses simplified speed-ratio approach. Phase 2 enhancement: detect motion type from speed and sign-crossing flags, then apply this 8-tier lookup table. Engine spec reference only.

interpretation.summary: Retrograde motion confers maximum Cheshta Bala (60). A stationary planet paradoxically scores low (15). Fast-moving plan
interpretation.detailed: Applies to starry planets (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn). Eight motion types with Virupa awards: Vakra (Retrogression) = 60. Anuvakra (Entering previous sign in retrograde) = 30. Vikala (Stationary/devoid of motion) = 15. Manda (Slower than normal) = 30. Mandatara (Slower than Manda) = 15. Sama (Somewhat increasing in motion) = 7.5. Chara (Faster than mean) = 45. Atichara (Entering next sign in accelerated motion) = 30. Effect: Retrograde motion confers maximum Cheshta Bala (60). A stationary planet paradoxically scores low (15). Fast-moving planets near their mean speed score moderately. This table is the canonical lookup for precise Cheshta Bala — more granular than the simplified speed-ratio.

condition.yoga_name: Cheshta Kendra — Mathematical Derivation of Motional Angle

yoga_check.description: Requires Seeghrocha (planetary apogee) data from Swiss Ephemeris. Phase 2: access swe.calc_ut with additional flags for apogee longitude per planet. Engine spec reference only.

interpretation.summary: The precise BPHS formula for deriving motional strength from a planet's relationship to its apogee. A planet at Cheshta
interpretation.detailed: For starry planets. Procedure: 1. Average the planet's Mean Longitude and True Longitude. 2. Deduct this average from the planet's Seeghrocha (Apogee).    Result = Cheshta Kendra. 3. If Cheshta Kendra > 180°, deduct from 360°. 4. Divide final value in degrees by 3 = Cheshta Bala Virupas. Applicable planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn. Effect: The precise BPHS formula for deriving motional strength from a planet's relationship to its apogee. A planet at Cheshta Kendra = 0° or 360° scores 0; at 180° from apogee scores maximum 60 Virupas.

full_text_passages.text: For starry planets. Procedure: 1. Average the planet's Mean Longitude and True Longitude. 2. Deduct this average from the planet's Seeghrocha (Apogee). condition.yoga_name: Drig Bala — Aspectual Strength

yoga_check.description: Implemented in vedic_calculator._drik_bala() using simplified Parashari aspect model. Full Drishti Pinda with partial aspect values per degree is a Phase 2 enhancement. Engine spec reference.

interpretation.summary: Measures the net quality of planetary influences received. A planet heavily aspected by benefics gains positive Drig Bal
interpretation.detailed: Sum of all aspectual influences received by a planet. For each aspecting planet: deduct 1/4 of the Drishti Pinda (aspect value) for malefic aspects; add 1/4 for benefic aspects. Super-addition: add the FULL aspect value of Mercury and Jupiter's aspects (not just 1/4). Net sum = Drig Bala in Virupas. Can be negative (net malefic pressure). Effect: Measures the net quality of planetary influences received. A planet heavily aspected by benefics gains positive Drig Bala; malefic aspects reduce it. Jupiter and Mercury aspects are doubly weighted in this calculation.

condition.yoga_name: Yuddha Bala — Planetary War Strength Redistribution

yoga_check.description: Implemented as _yuddha_bala() stub returning 0 for all planets. Full implementation: detect pairs within 1° longitude, compare preliminary Shadbalas, redistribute difference. Staged simplification per commission brief. Phase 2 enhancement.

interpretation.summary: Planetary war amplifies the strong planet and further weakens the defeated planet. A planet vanquished in war loses Shad
interpretation.detailed: Applies when two starry planets (Mars through Saturn) are within 1° of each other (Yuddha / Planetary War). The victor is determined by the planet with greater total Shadbala at that moment. Rule: the difference between the two planets' total Shadbalas is added to the victor's score and deducted from the vanquished planet's score. Sun, Moon, Rahu, and Ketu are exempt from Yuddha. Effect: Planetary war amplifies the strong planet and further weakens the defeated planet. A planet vanquished in war loses Shadbala and correspondingly weakens its significations during its dashas.

condition.yoga_name: Ahargana Derivation — Varsha and Maasa Lord Calculation

yoga_check.description: Current engine uses _find_previous_mesha_sankranti_jd() and _find_previous_new_moon_jd() for Varsha and Maasa lords — equivalent to Ahargana approach. Engine spec reference only.

interpretation.summary: Provides the exact mathematical derivation for the temporal lordship multipliers. The current engine approximates Varsha
interpretation.detailed: Determines which planet receives the Varsha (Year) and Maasa (Month) temporal multipliers using day-count from creation (Ahargana). Varsha Lord: divide Ahargana by 360; multiply completed years by 3, add 1, divide by 7 — remainder is weekday index for Varsha lord. Maasa Lord: divide Ahargana by 30; multiply completed months by 2, add 1, divide by 7 — remainder is weekday index for Maasa lord. Dina Lord: Ahargana mod 7 = weekday index (Sunday=0, Saturday=6). Weekday sequence: Sun/Moon/Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn. Effect: Provides the exact mathematical derivation for the temporal lordship multipliers. The current engine approximates Varsha lord from Mesha Sankranti (Sun's Aries ingress) and Maasa lord from the preceding new moon, which is equivalent in effect.

interpretation.summary: The directional gate determines whether a planet's distance from the equinox adds to or subtracts from Ayana Bala. Sun i
interpretation.detailed: Precise directional gate for Ayana Bala declination (Kranti): Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Venus → Northern declination (Uttara Kranti) = PLUS. Moon, Saturn → Southern declination (Dakshina Kranti) = PLUS. Mercury → any direction = always PLUS. Opposite conditions = MINUS for all except Mercury. Super-modifier: Sun's final Ayana Bala product is always multiplied by 2. Mercury exception: gains strength from any declination (always PLUS). Effect: The directional gate determines whether a planet's distance from the equinox adds to or subtracts from Ayana Bala. Sun in Northern declination is doubly empowered (standard gain × 2). Mercury ignores direction entirely.
